2.3 million blocks. About 26 years. Here's how the Great Pyramid was built, in 40 seconds. ⏱️

Copper tools and wet wooden wedges to split stone. Sledges dragged over wet sand. Granite floated 900 km down the Nile.

And the twist: it didn't look like this. It was covered in polished white limestone that shone in the sun. ✨

Next: the Empire State Building, in 410 days. Follow so you don't miss it. 👇

yt_title: How the Great Pyramid Was Built: 26 Years in 40 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
2.3 million blocks, about 6 million tonnes. Copper tools and wooden wedges to split limestone, sledges over wet sand, granite shipped 900+ km from Aswan for the King's Chamber, and a casing of polished white Tura limestone that once made it shine.

The Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu, c. 2600 BC), the tallest human-made structure for ~3,700 years, built in 40 seconds.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza
Construction methods are debated; figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
